intent.raw_query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter 2026 from LAX

experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Experience
experiences.description: Explore the magnificent 14th-century Gyeongbokgung Palace while dressed in a traditional Hanbok rented from nearby shops. Wearing Hanbok grants free palace entry. Watch the royal guard-changing ceremony and visit the National Folk Museum of Korea within the palace grounds for deep immersion into Korean royal culture and history.

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into one of Seoul's oldest and most beloved traditional markets. Sample iconic Korean street foods including bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (addictive mini rice rolls), tteokbokki (spicy rice cakes), and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare). Interact with local vendors and experience the vibrant, authentic atmosphere of everyday Korean food culture.

experiences.name: K-Pop & Hallyu Culture Tour in Gangnam
experiences.description: Explore the heartbeat of K-Pop culture in Gangnam. Visit SM Town COEX Artium, browse K-Pop merchandise stores, and stop at the famous SMTOWN Museum. Walk through Apgujeong Rodeo Street where many K-Pop idols frequent, and visit the K-Star Road featuring character statues of top idol groups. End with a visit to a K-Pop themed café for themed drinks and photo opportunities.

experiences.name: Korean Temple Stay & Meditation at Jogyesa Temple
experiences.description: Participate in a half-day temple life program at Jogyesa Temple, the center of Korean Buddhism in Seoul. Experience templestay activities including meditation, tea ceremony, Buddhist lantern making, and a monk-guided tour. Gain insight into Korean spiritual culture and enjoy a moment of tranquility in the middle of the bustling city. A deeply authentic and reflective cultural experience.

experiences.name: Korean BBQ & Makgeolli Pairing Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class where you learn to prepare classic Korean BBQ dishes including samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly) and bulgogi (marinated beef), alongside traditional side dishes (banchan). Learn the art of pairing dishes with makgeolli (traditional rice wine). Taught by a local chef, this experience blends culinary skill with cultural storytelling about Korean dining etiquette and food history.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Seoul, South Korea
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Travel from Incheon International Airport to hotel via AREX (Airport Railroad Express) to Hongik University Station, then transfer to Line 3 toward Gyeongbokgung Station. Journey takes approximately 60–75 minutes. Cost: ~₩4,150 KRW.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Boutique Stay in Gyeongbokgung, Jongno-gu. After freshening up, take a short walk to nearby Gyeongbokgung Palace exterior to get oriented with the neighborhood. Explore Bukchon Hanok Village (a 15-minute walk) — stroll the traditional alleyways, admire the hanok architecture, and soak in the atmosphere. Free entry to the village streets.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Insadong Street (10-minute walk from hotel) for your first evening in Seoul. Browse traditional craft shops, street stalls, and the Ssamziegil courtyard complex. Pick up a hotteok (sweet pancake) from a street vendor for ₩1,500.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick snack at Incheon Airport (convenience store kimbap ~₩1,500–₩2,000)
meals.lunch: No lunch scheduled due to travel — grab a convenience store meal (GS25 or CU) near the hotel upon arrival: triangle kimbap + ramyeon ~₩3,000
meals.dinner: Tosokchon Samgyetang area or a nearby Insadong pojangmacha (street food tent): tteokbokki + sundae + eomuk set ~₩6,000–₩8,000

day_by_day.notes: Get a T-money card at Incheon Airport or any convenience store (₩2,500 deposit + load funds). This card is essential for all buses and subways. Exchange some cash at the airport — rates are decent at the official exchange counters. Dress warmly — December in Seoul is cold (0°C to -5°C typical).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeongbokgung Palace (opens 9:00 AM, 5-minute walk from hotel). Admission: ₩3,000. Watch the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at 10:00 AM at the main gate (Gwanghwamun Gate). Explore the palace grounds including Geunjeongjeon (throne hall) and Gyeonghoeru Pavilion. Rent a hanbok for free entry and beautiful photos (~₩15,000–₩20,000 for 2 hours at nearby rental shops).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the National Folk Museum of Korea (inside Gyeongbokgung grounds — free entry). Explore exhibits on traditional Korean life, customs, and history. Afterward, visit Cheong Wa Dae (Blue House) — the former presidential residence opened to public tours (book free tickets online in advance at www.opencheongwadae.kr).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gwanghwamun Square for evening strolls and to see the Yi Sun-sin and King Sejong statues lit up at night. Then explore the underground Gwanghwamun Station shopping arcade for warmth and budget shopping.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast near hotel: banana milk + egg sandwich ~₩2,500 or find a local 해장국 (haejangguk) restaurant for a hangover soup breakfast ~₩7,000
meals.lunch: Tosokchon Samgyetang (famous ginseng chicken soup near Gyeongbokgung) ~₩17,000 — worth the splurge for an iconic dish, or opt for a nearby bunsik (snack) restaurant: bibimbap ~₩7,000–₩8,000
meals.dinner: Gwanghwamun area: Jongno 3-ga pojangmacha alley — grilled skewers, pajeon (scallion pancake), and makgeolli (rice wine). Budget ~₩10,000–₩15,000 for food and a drink

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays — since today is Wednesday, it's open. Wear your warmest layers. The palace grounds are large — wear comfortable shoes. Hanbok rental shops are clustered on the east side of the palace near the ticket booth.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and the Secret Garden (Huwon). Admission: ₩3,000 (palace) + ₩5,000 (Secret Garden guided tour — book online). The Secret Garden tour runs at set times and lasts about 90 minutes through beautiful forested grounds. Take Line 3 from Gyeongbokgung to Anguk Station (1 stop, ₩1,400).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Changgyeonggung Palace next door (₩1,000 admission) and walk through the connected grounds to Jongmyo Shrine — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the royal ancestral shrine. Admission: ₩1,000. The serene, minimalist architecture is striking in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to Jongno 3-ga area and explore the famous Pimatgol Alley — a historic back alley with cheap, traditional Korean eateries. Then visit Tapgol Park (free), Seoul's first modern park, to see the 10-story marble pagoda and murals depicting the March 1st Independence Movement.

meals.breakfast: Nearby local bakery or Paris Baguette near hotel: coffee + pastry ~₩4,000–₩5,000
meals.lunch: Ikseon-dong Hanok Village (5-minute walk from Changdeokgung): trendy but affordable fusion cafes and Korean lunch sets ~₩8,000–₩12,000. Try the area's famous donut or tteok (rice cake) shops.
meals.dinner: Pimatgol Alley, Jongno: 순대국밥 (sundae gukbap / sausage soup rice) ~₩7,000 or 설렁탕 (seolleongtang / ox bone soup) ~₩9,000 — hearty and warming for cold December nights

day_by_day.notes: Secret Garden tours have limited capacity — book ahead online at the Changdeokgung official website. Jongmyo Shrine has free entry on the last Wednesday of each month. Ikseon-dong is a beautifully preserved hanok neighborhood that's very Instagrammable and worth exploring slowly.

day_by_day.morning: Take subway Line 4 to Myeongdong Station (from Gyeongbokgung: Line 3 to Chungmuro, transfer to Line 4, ~20 min, ₩1,400). Visit Myeongdong Cathedral (free, open to visitors) — a stunning Gothic-style Catholic cathedral and one of Korea's most important religious sites. Then explore the surrounding streets before the shopping crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Namdaemun Market (10-minute walk from Myeongdong) — one of Korea's oldest and largest traditional markets. Browse stalls selling everything from clothing to kitchenware. Must-try street foods: hotteok, gimbap, bindaetteok (mung bean pancake). Then visit Sungnyemun Gate (Namdaemun Gate) — the iconic Great South Gate of Seoul (free, outdoor).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Myeongdong for the famous evening street food market. Stalls open up from around 5 PM. Try: cheese lobster, tornado potato, giant skewers, Korean corn dogs. Budget ₩10,000–₩15,000 for a full street food dinner. Browse K-beauty shops for affordable skincare (Innisfree, The Face Shop, Etude House — all budget-friendly).

meals.breakfast: Hotel area: find a local 김밥천국 (Kimbap Cheonguk) style restaurant — kimbap + soup combo ~₩5,000–₩6,000
meals.lunch: Namdaemun Market: bindaetteok (mung bean pancake) + makgeolli at a market pojangmacha ~₩8,000–₩10,000
meals.dinner: Myeongdong street food stalls: mix and match — budget ₩10,000–₩15,000 for a satisfying street food dinner

day_by_day.notes: Myeongdong street food is best experienced in the evening when all stalls are open. K-beauty products here are cheaper than at airport duty-free for some items. Namdaemun Market is best explored on foot — it's a maze of alleys so allow plenty of time. Keep your belongings secure in crowded areas.

day_by_day.morning: Take subway to Hongdae (Hongik University) area — Line 3 from Gyeongbokgung to Dongdaemun History & Culture Park, transfer to Line 2 to Hongik University Station (~35 min, ₩1,500). Explore Hongdae's vibrant streets, murals, and independent shops in the morning when it's less crowded. Visit Gyeongui Line Forest Park (free) — a beautiful linear park built on an old railway line.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to nearby Sinchon and Ewha Womans University area (1 stop on Line 2). Explore Ewha's beautiful campus (free entry) and the surrounding shopping streets with affordable fashion and accessories. Walk back through Hongdae for street performances (especially on weekends) and indie music culture.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Hongdae for the famous Saturday night K-indie music scene. Check out free busking performances near Exit 9 of Hongik University Station (usually starts around 7–8 PM). Explore the club and bar street — many venues have free or cheap entry before midnight.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area before departing: convenience store or local 해장국 restaurant ~₩5,000–₩7,000
meals.lunch: Hongdae area: 연남동 (Yeonnamdong) neighborhood nearby has affordable cafes and restaurants. Try a Korean set meal (백반/baekban) ~₩8,000–₩10,000 or a popular local ramen shop ~₩7,000
meals.dinner: Hongdae: 닭갈비 (dak-galbi / spicy stir-fried chicken) — a fun, communal dish cooked at the table. Look for budget restaurants near the university. ~₩10,000–₩13,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Hongdae is Seoul's youth culture hub — street art, indie music, K-pop dance covers, and vibrant nightlife all coexist here. Saturday is the best day to visit for maximum energy. The Gyeongui Line Forest Park is lovely even in winter. Yeonnamdong (just north of Hongdae) is a quieter, hip neighborhood worth exploring.

day_by_day.morning: Visit N Seoul Tower on Namsan Mountain. Take bus 02 (Namsan Circular Bus) from Chungmuro Station or hike up Namsan (free, about 40 minutes). N Seoul Tower observation deck: ₩16,000 (or just enjoy the view from the outdoor terrace for free). See the famous love lock fence. Best morning views of the city on a clear winter day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend Namsan and head to Itaewon (nearby, Line 6). Explore the multicultural neighborhood — international food, vintage clothing shops, and Antique Furniture Street. Visit Leeum Samsung Museum of Art (Line 6 Hangangjin Station) — admission ~₩10,000 for a world-class contemporary art collection in a stunning building.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Haebangchon (HBC) neighborhood adjacent to Itaewon — a quieter, artsy neighborhood with affordable international restaurants and cozy bars. Great for a relaxed Sunday evening with a mix of locals and expats.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area: 순두부찌개 (soft tofu stew) at a local restaurant ~₩7,000–₩8,000 — perfect warming winter breakfast
meals.lunch: Itaewon: budget international food — try a Middle Eastern shawarma wrap ~₩7,000 or Vietnamese pho ~₩8,000 for a change of pace
meals.dinner: Haebangchon: affordable Thai, Mexican, or Italian restaurants with generous portions ~₩10,000–₩13,000, or find a local Korean 삼겹살 (samgyeopsal) restaurant — pork belly BBQ ~₩12,000–₩15,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Check weather before visiting N Seoul Tower — clear winter days offer spectacular views but foggy or smoggy days can be disappointing. The Namsan hike is manageable but wear sturdy shoes as paths may be icy in December. Itaewon has the best international food variety in Seoul if you need a break from Korean cuisine.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Bukhansan National Park — Seoul's mountain park within city limits. Take Line 3 to Gupabal Station, then bus to Bukhansan Ui Station or directly to a trailhead. Hike the Baegundae Peak trail (8.5 km round trip, 4–5 hours) or a shorter trail like Dobongsan for spectacular rocky mountain views above the city. Free entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the hike or descend and explore the Bukhansanseong (Fortress Wall) trail — ancient fortress walls winding through the mountains. The combination of winter scenery, rocky peaks, and fortress ruins is stunning and uniquely Korean.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Seoul and head to Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — a futuristic Zaha Hadid-designed building (free to walk around outside, some exhibitions inside). The surrounding Dongdaemun area lights up beautifully at night. Explore Dongdaemun Market for late-night shopping.

meals.breakfast: Pack a convenience store breakfast to eat before or during the hike: triangle kimbap + banana milk + energy bar ~₩4,000
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch for the mountain: convenience store kimbap roll + instant ramen from a mountain shelter (many trailhead areas have small restaurants selling ramen ~₩4,000–₩5,000)
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun area: 닭한마리 (dak hanmari / whole chicken soup) — a Dongdaemun specialty. Famous alley of restaurants near Dongdaemun Station. ~₩13,000–₩15,000 per person, very filling

day_by_day.notes: Bukhansan in December can have icy trails — bring hiking poles if possible, or rent them near trailheads (~₩3,000). Wear waterproof boots and many layers. Start the hike early (by 9 AM) to avoid rushing descent in early winter darkness (sunset around 5:15 PM). The DDP is free to walk around and photograph at night.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Seochon Village (서촌) — the charming neighborhood west of Gyeongbokgung Palace, just a short walk from your hotel. This area was home to artists and intellectuals historically and retains its traditional alley character. Visit Cheongun-dong Gyegan Stream, browse independent bookshops, art galleries, and traditional tea houses.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Sajik Park (free) — a serene hilltop park near the hotel with great views and historical significance. Then visit the National Palace Museum of Korea (inside Gyeongbokgung grounds, free admission) — excellent collection of royal artifacts, furniture, and art from the Joseon Dynasty.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Cheonggyecheon Stream (청계천) — a beautifully restored urban stream running through central Seoul. Take Line 1 or 5 to Gwanghwamun or City Hall area. Walk along the illuminated stream path (free, about 2–3 km scenic walk). In December there are often winter light festivals along the stream.

meals.breakfast: Seochon Village: find a traditional 죽 (juk / rice porridge) restaurant — a light, healthy Korean breakfast ~₩6,000–₩8,000
meals.lunch: Seochon area: 칼국수 (kalguksu / knife-cut noodle soup) at a local neighborhood restaurant ~₩7,000–₩8,000
meals.dinner: Near Cheonggyecheon: explore the Jongno area for 부대찌개 (budae jjigae / army stew) — a hearty, budget-friendly fusion stew ~₩9,000–₩11,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Seochon is often overlooked by tourists in favor of Bukchon but is equally charming and less crowded. The Cheonggyecheon Stream walk is especially magical in winter with Christmas and winter light decorations. The stream is free to access at any point along its 8 km length.

day_by_day.morning: Take subway to Insadong (Line 3 Anguk Station, 1 stop from Gyeongbokgung) for a deeper exploration. Visit Jogyesa Temple (free) — the head temple of Korean Buddhism, beautifully decorated with lanterns, especially festive in December. Attend a morning prayer ceremony if timing allows (usually 4 AM and 10 AM).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Insadong antique and craft market streets in depth. Visit Ssamziegil (free entry to the courtyard) — an indie shopping complex with unique Korean crafts, handmade goods, and street food. Browse traditional hanji (Korean paper) shops, ink brush sets, and celadon ceramics — great for affordable souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Nakwon Instrument Arcade (낙원상가) nearby — a multi-story building filled with music instrument shops, a fascinating slice of Seoul subculture. Then visit the Jongno Tower area and walk to Bosingak Bell Pavilion — the site of Seoul's famous New Year's bell ringing ceremony (great to see in advance).

meals.breakfast: Hotel area or Insadong: traditional 쌍화차 (ssanghwacha / herbal tea) and 약과 (yakgwa / honey cookies) at a traditional tea house ~₩5,000–₩7,000
meals.lunch: Insadong: 비빔밥 (bibimbap) at a traditional Korean restaurant ~₩9,000–₩11,000 or street food from Ssamziegil stalls ~₩5,000–₩7,000
meals.dinner: Jongno area: 곱창 (gopchang / grilled intestines) — a local specialty and very affordable at street-level restaurants ~₩10,000–₩12,000, or 삼겹살 BBQ at a budget KBBQ spot ~₩12,000–₩15,000

day_by_day.notes: Jogyesa Temple is free and one of Seoul's most important cultural sites. The paper lotus lanterns hanging from trees are beautiful year-round. Insadong is the best place in Seoul for traditional Korean souvenirs at reasonable prices — much better value than airport shops. Good day to do souvenir shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress — a UNESCO World Heritage Site just 1 hour from Seoul. Take subway Line 1 from Jonggak Station to Suwon Station (~55 min, ₩2,600). Walk 15 minutes or take a short bus to the fortress. Admission: ₩1,000. Walk the entire 5.7 km fortress wall circuit for panoramic views of the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Suwon's Paldalmun Gate and the surrounding traditional market area. Visit the Hwaseong Haenggung Palace (temporary palace, ₩1,500 admission) inside the fortress walls. Try the local specialty — 왕갈비 (wang galbi / king-sized grilled ribs) that Suwon is famous for.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul for Christmas Eve celebrations. Head to Myeongdong Cathedral for the Christmas Eve midnight mass (or evening services — one of Seoul's most atmospheric Christmas experiences, free). Myeongdong streets are beautifully decorated and buzzing with Christmas energy.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area before departing: quick convenience store meal or local restaurant ~₩4,000–₩6,000
meals.lunch: Suwon: 왕갈비 (Suwon-style wang galbi) — the city's most famous dish. Look for restaurants near Paldalmun Gate. Budget ₩15,000–₩18,000 (a worthy splurge for a regional specialty)
meals.dinner: Myeongdong Christmas Eve: street food and festive atmosphere. Budget ₩10,000–₩15,000 for street food dinner, or find a budget Korean restaurant in the area ~₩8,000–₩10,000

day_by_day.notes: Suwon Hwaseong is one of the most impressive historical sites near Seoul and often skipped by tourists — highly recommended. The fortress walk takes 2–3 hours at a leisurely pace. Christmas in Seoul is festive and commercialized — Myeongdong and Hongdae are the liveliest areas. Myeongdong Cathedral Christmas Eve service is a cultural experience worth attending even for non-Christians.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Korea (국립중앙박물관) — one of the world's largest museums with an incredible collection of Korean art and history. Take Line 4 to Ichon Station (about 25 min from Gyeongbokgung, ₩1,400). Free admission to the permanent collection. Spend 2–3 hours exploring 12,000 years of Korean history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to adjacent Yongsan Family Park (free) for a winter stroll, then head to the War Memorial of Korea (전쟁기념관) nearby — free admission. A sobering but important museum covering Korean military history from ancient times through the Korean War. The outdoor exhibits with tanks, aircraft, and ships are impressive.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Hangang River Park (한강공원) — Yeouido section (Line 5 to Yeouido Station). Walk along the river and enjoy the city skyline at night. In December, there may be winter festivals or ice skating rinks set up along the river. Ice skating: ~₩1,000 entry + ₩5,000 skate rental.

meals.breakfast: Christmas morning treat: find a nice bakery near the hotel for a festive breakfast — coffee + pastries ~₩6,000–₩8,000
meals.lunch: Museum cafeteria at National Museum of Korea: affordable Korean set meals ~₩7,000–₩9,000, or bring packed snacks
meals.dinner: Yeouido area: 치킨 (Korean fried chicken) — a Christmas tradition in Korea! Koreans eat fried chicken on Christmas. Order from a local chicken shop or find a 치킨 restaurant ~₩18,000–₩22,000 for a whole chicken (shareable). Pair with beer for the classic 치맥 experience.

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Day (December 25) is a public holiday in South Korea — most attractions are open but some smaller shops may be closed. The 치킨 (fried chicken) on Christmas is a genuine Korean cultural tradition — embrace it! The National Museum of Korea is world-class and completely free for permanent exhibitions — don't skip it. Yeouido Hangang Park may have a winter festival or outdoor skating rink — check Seoul's official tourism website closer to the date.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Gangnam district — take Line 3 from Gyeongbokgung to Apgujeong Station (~30 min, ₩1,500). Walk along Apgujeong Rodeo Street and explore the upscale neighborhood. Visit the free COEX Starfield Library (Line 2 Samseong Station) — a stunning public library inside the COEX mall with towering bookshelves. Free entry and very photogenic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Bongeunsa Temple (봉은사) — a 1,200-year-old Buddhist temple in the heart of Gangnam, free admission. A peaceful contrast to the surrounding luxury district. Then explore the COEX Mall (free entry) — one of Asia's largest underground malls, great for warmth and window shopping. Visit the K-pop merchandise stores inside.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Garosu-gil (가로수길) — a tree-lined boulevard in Sinsa-dong with boutique shops, cafes, and restaurants. Beautiful even in winter. Then explore nearby Seolleung Park (free) — the UNESCO-listed royal tombs of Joseon kings in the middle of Gangnam. Lit up softly at night.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area: 해장국 (haejangguk) or 설렁탕 (seolleongtang) at a local restaurant ~₩8,000–₩9,000
meals.lunch: Gangnam area: find a 분식 (bunsik) snack restaurant for affordable comfort food — 떡볶이 + 순대 + 튀김 set ~₩7,000–₩8,000, or a budget 한식 (hansik) restaurant ~₩8,000–₩10,000
meals.dinner: Garosu-gil: browse the restaurant options — try a cozy Korean BBQ spot or a modern 한정식 (hanjeongsik / Korean set meal) at a mid-range restaurant ~₩12,000–₩15,000 for a special last full evening meal

day_by_day.notes: Gangnam is Seoul's upscale district but has plenty of free sights and affordable food options. The COEX Starfield Library is one of Seoul's most Instagrammable spots — free and open to all. Bongeunsa Temple offers free templestay introductory programs on some days — check their website. Garosu-gil is best in the evening when the cafes and restaurants are lit up warmly.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Seoul. Take one last walk through Gyeongbokgung neighborhood — visit the nearby Sajik Park for a quiet morning stroll and final views of the area around your hotel. Stop by a local 시장 (sijang / traditional market) — Tongin Market (통인시장, 10-minute walk) is a beloved local market where you can use old Korean coins (엽전) to pick up small dishes from different stalls (coin lunch box experience ~₩5,000).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of hotel and head to Incheon Airport. Take AREX from Hongik University Station or Seoul Station. Allow at least 3 hours before your flight. At the airport, use any remaining Korean won at duty-free shops or airport restaurants. The AREX express train from Seoul Station to Incheon takes 43 minutes (~₩9,500) or the all-stop train takes 66 minutes (~₩4,150).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon International Airport.

meals.breakfast: Tongin Market coin lunch box experience: collect traditional Korean side dishes with coin tokens ~₩5,000–₩7,000 — a uniquely local final breakfast experience
meals.lunch: Airport meal: Korean airport restaurants — 비빔밥 (bibimbap) or 삼겹살 sets available airside ~₩10,000–₩14,000. Or use remaining won at a convenience store for a budget airport snack
meals.dinner: On the flight

day_by_day.notes: Tongin Market coin lunch box is a wonderful final Seoul experience — very local and affordable. Exchange remaining Korean won back to your home currency at the airport (rates are acceptable). Keep ₩10,000–₩15,000 in cash for the AREX train and any last-minute needs. The T-money card can be refunded at the airport (deposit + remaining balance returned at customer service desks). Safe travels!

trip_options.title: Classic Seoul, South Korea Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – In transit. Flight LH lands at Incheon International Airport at 13:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Clear immigration and baggage claim, then take the AREX Express Train (~43 min) or limousine bus to central Seoul. Check in to the Boutique Stay in Gyeongbokgung, Jongno-gu and freshen up. Take a gentle orientation stroll along Gyeongbokgung Palace's outer walls and the charming Bukchon Hanok Village entrance streets to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Insadong Street (10-min walk from hotel) – browse traditional Korean craft shops, tea houses, and street snack stalls. Enjoy the festive December atmosphere and pick up a warm hotteok (sweet pancake) from a street vendor.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Incheon Airport food court – try bibimbap or kimbap (~₩8,000–12,000)
meals.dinner: Tosokchon Samgyetang (토속촌 삼계탕) near Gyeongbokgung – iconic ginseng chicken soup, perfect for warming up after travel (~₩18,000–22,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: December in Seoul is cold (avg -2°C to 5°C). Pack thermal layers, a heavy coat, gloves, and a scarf. Get a T-money card at the airport for seamless subway and bus travel. Exchange some currency or withdraw KRW at the airport for convenience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeongbokgung Palace (경복궁) – just steps from your hotel. Arrive early (~9:00 AM) to catch the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at the main gate (Gwanghwamun). Explore the grand throne hall Geunjeongjeon, the serene Gyeonghoeru Pavilion, and the National Folk Museum of Korea within the palace grounds. Consider renting a hanbok (traditional dress) for free palace entry and beautiful winter photos (~₩15,000–25,000 for 2-hour rental).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the National Palace Museum of Korea (free entry) adjacent to Gyeongbokgung for deeper historical context. Afterward, head to Bukchon Hanok Village (북촌한옥마을) – wander the narrow alleyways lined with traditional wooden hanok houses. Stop at viewpoint 2 on Gahoe-ro for iconic Seoul skyline photos.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Samcheongdong-gil (삼청동길) – a trendy street with indie cafés, galleries, and boutique shops. Browse the art galleries and enjoy the cozy winter ambiance.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby café – try patbingsu or hotteok from a Samcheongdong street stall (~₩3,000–7,000)
meals.lunch: Gwanghwamun Gukbap (광화문국밥) near the palace – hearty pork rice soup, a Seoul classic (~₩10,000–13,000)
meals.dinner: Samcheongdong Sujebi – traditional hand-torn noodle soup restaurant in the Samcheongdong area (~₩10,000–15,000)

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung Palace is closed on Tuesdays; since today is Wednesday it is open. The hanbok rental shops are clustered near the palace's east gate. Wear comfortable walking shoes – the hanok village involves uphill cobblestone paths.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace (창덕궁) and its UNESCO-listed Secret Garden (Huwon) – book the Secret Garden tour in advance online (~₩8,000). The snow-dusted garden in December is breathtaking. Then explore the adjacent Changgyeonggung Palace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk south to Jongmyo Shrine (종묘) – a serene Confucian royal ancestral shrine and UNESCO World Heritage Site (₩1,000 entry). Afterward, explore the Ikseon-dong Hanok Village (익선동) – a hip, renovated hanok neighborhood with quirky cafés, vintage shops, and fusion eateries, popular with young Koreans.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Cheonggyecheon Stream (청계천) for a romantic evening walk along the illuminated waterway – beautifully lit in winter. End the evening at Gwangjang Market (광장시장) for a vibrant street food experience.

meals.breakfast: Café in Ikseon-dong area – try Korean-style toast (계란토스트) and barley tea (~₩5,000–8,000)
meals.lunch: Light meal near Changdeokgung – doenjang jjigae (fermented soybean paste stew) set at a local restaurant (~₩9,000–13,000)
meals.dinner: Gwangjang Market (광장시장) – must-try bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak kimbap (addictive mini rolls), and tteokbokki (~₩10,000–15,000 for a full street food spread)

day_by_day.notes: Jongmyo Shrine has limited independent access – guided tours run at set times. Check the official website for the English tour schedule. Gwangjang Market is especially lively in the evening and is one of Seoul's oldest and most authentic markets.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Itaewon/Haebangchon area and visit the National Museum of Korea (국립중앙박물관) – one of Asia's largest museums with an outstanding collection of Korean art and artifacts (free entry). Spend 2–3 hours exploring the permanent collection.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Namsan Mountain and N Seoul Tower (남산타워). Take the cable car up (~₩9,500 round trip) or hike the scenic trail (30–40 min walk). Enjoy panoramic winter views of Seoul from the observation deck (~₩21,000). Visit the famous love lock fence. The tower is especially magical as dusk falls over the city.
day_by_day.evening: Descend to Myeongdong (명동) – Seoul's busiest shopping and street food district. Browse K-beauty shops (Innisfree, Etude House, Olive Young), sample street food, and soak in the electric atmosphere. December often features Christmas decorations and markets here.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or nearby bakery – Paris Baguette or Tous Les Jours for pastries and coffee (~₩5,000–8,000)
meals.lunch: Museum cafeteria or nearby restaurant – try dosirak (Korean lunch box set) (~₩10,000–14,000)
meals.dinner: Myeongdong Kyoja (명동교자) – legendary hand-made kalguksu (knife-cut noodles) and mandu (dumplings), always a queue but worth it (~₩11,000–14,000)

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Korea is closed on Mondays – open today. Book N Seoul Tower tickets online in advance to avoid queues, especially on a Friday evening. Myeongdong is extremely crowded on Friday nights – keep belongings secure.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the DMZ (Demilitarized Zone) – book a half-day or full-day DMZ tour from central Seoul (~₩50,000–80,000 per person including transport). Visit the 3rd Infiltration Tunnel, Dora Observatory, and Dorasan Station. A sobering and historically significant experience that provides deep insight into Korea's divided history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Seoul by early-to-mid afternoon. Rest briefly at the hotel, then explore the Seochon Village (서촌마을) – the charming neighborhood west of Gyeongbokgung, full of independent art studios, traditional tea houses, and literary history (poet Yun Dong-ju lived here).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional Korean cultural performance – check the Korean House (한국의집) near Namsan for dinner performances featuring traditional music, dance, and a multi-course hanjeonsik meal (~₩80,000–120,000 for dinner show, book in advance). Alternatively, catch a B-boy performance at the Nanta Theatre.

meals.breakfast: Early start – grab kimbap and a warm drink from a convenience store (GS25 or CU) before the DMZ tour (~₩3,000–5,000)
meals.lunch: Included in most DMZ tour packages, or eat near Dorasan Station
meals.dinner: Korean House dinner performance or Seochon area restaurant – try a hearty sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) set (~₩12,000–16,000) if skipping the performance

day_by_day.notes: DMZ tours must be booked at least 1–2 days in advance; passport is required. Tours depart early (typically 7:00–8:00 AM) from central Seoul. Saturday evening cultural performances are popular – advance booking is essential.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple (조계사) – the head temple of Korean Buddhism, located in Jongno-gu, a 10-minute walk from the hotel. The December lantern decorations are stunning. Attend a morning ceremony if interested (free). Explore the surrounding Insa-dong area's antique shops and traditional tea houses.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP – 동대문디자인플라자) – the futuristic landmark designed by Zaha Hadid. Explore the design exhibitions (~₩2,000–5,000 depending on exhibit), the outdoor plaza, and the surrounding fashion district. Browse the massive Doota and Migliore shopping malls for K-fashion.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in the Dongdaemun area for its legendary late-night energy. The wholesale fashion markets (Dongdaemun Market) open in the evening and stay busy until dawn – a uniquely Korean experience. Browse fabrics, accessories, and street fashion.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Korean breakfast at a local sikdang (식당) near Jogyesa – doenjang jjigae with rice and banchan (~₩8,000–12,000)
meals.lunch: Insadong area – try a traditional Korean tea house lunch set with tteok (rice cakes) and seasonal tea (~₩12,000–18,000)
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun area pojangmacha (street food tent) – grilled skewers (꼬치), tteokbokki, and odeng (fish cake soup) (~₩8,000–12,000)

day_by_day.notes: Jogyesa Temple is free to visit. The DDP is particularly photogenic at night with its LED rose garden installation (seasonal). Sunday is a great day for Insadong as local artisan markets set up along the main street.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the trendy Hongdae (홍대) neighborhood – the epicenter of Korean indie music, street art, and youth culture. Visit the vibrant street art murals around Hongik University, browse the unique shops along Eoulmadang-ro, and check out the flea market (weekends) or indie record shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short bus to Sinchon and Ewha Womans University area – explore the eclectic shopping streets and the stunning Ewha campus. Then head to the nearby Han River (한강) Yeouido Park. Rent a bicycle (~₩3,000/hour) and cycle along the frozen riverbank, or simply enjoy the winter scenery and Han River views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hongdae for its legendary nightlife and K-indie music scene. Catch a live performance at a small club or busker performance on the main street. December often features special holiday live music events.

meals.breakfast: Hongdae brunch café – Seoul's café culture is world-class; try a themed café for the full experience (~₩8,000–15,000)
meals.lunch: Yeonnam-dong (연남동) adjacent to Hongdae – a charming neighborhood with diverse international and fusion restaurants; try a Korean-Chinese jajangmyeon (black bean noodles) (~₩8,000–12,000)
meals.dinner: Hongdae area Korean BBQ – samgyeopsal (pork belly) at a local restaurant with soju (~₩15,000–25,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Monday note: National Museum of Korea is closed today – already visited on Friday. Hongdae is liveliest in the afternoon and evening. The area around Gyeongui Line Forest Park (경의선숲길) connecting Hongdae to Yeonnam-dong is great for a scenic winter walk.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeonghuigung Palace (경희궁) – a lesser-visited but beautiful palace near your hotel (free entry). Then explore the Seoul Museum of History (서울역사박물관) adjacent to it (free) for a comprehensive overview of Seoul's transformation from ancient capital to modern metropolis.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Gangnam (강남) – the upscale district made globally famous by Psy's 'Gangnam Style.' Visit the COEX Mall (코엑스몰) – Asia's largest underground shopping complex. Don't miss the stunning Starfield Library inside COEX – an Instagram-famous open library with towering bookshelves. Browse the aquarium or catch a K-pop exhibition if available.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Apgujeong Rodeo Street (압구정 로데오) and Cheongdam-dong – Seoul's luxury fashion district. Window-shop at high-end boutiques and visit the SM Entertainment building (K-pop agency HQ). End the evening at a trendy Gangnam rooftop bar or café.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or Seochon area bakery – warm porridge (죽, juk) from Bon Juk chain, a healthy Korean breakfast (~₩8,000–12,000)
meals.lunch: COEX food court – wide variety of Korean and Asian options (~₩10,000–15,000)
meals.dinner: Gangnam area – try galbi (grilled beef short ribs) at a mid-range Korean BBQ restaurant (~₩20,000–35,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung Palace is closed on Tuesdays – already visited on Day 2. COEX Starfield Library is free to enter and open to the public. The Gangnam district is a 30-minute subway ride from the hotel (Line 3 from Anguk or Gyeongbokgung station).

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress (수원화성) – a UNESCO World Heritage Site about 1 hour south of Seoul by subway (Line 1 from Seoul Station). The massive 18th-century fortress walls offer stunning winter walks. Visit Hwaseong Haenggung (행궁) – the royal palace within the fortress (~₩1,500).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Suwon's traditional market area around the fortress. Visit the Suwon Hwaseong Museum for historical context. Return to Seoul by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Evening at leisure in the Jongno area near your hotel. Explore the atmospheric Pimatgol Alley (피맛골) – a historic narrow alley with traditional Korean taverns (makgeolli bars). Experience a pojangmacha (street tent bar) culture with warm makgeolli (rice wine) and pajeon (scallion pancake).

meals.breakfast: Early Korean breakfast near hotel – haejang-guk (해장국, hangover soup/hearty morning soup) at a local restaurant (~₩9,000–13,000)
meals.lunch: Suwon's famous galbi (수원왕갈비) – Suwon is renowned for its large, flavorful beef short ribs; this is a must-try in the city (~₩25,000–35,000 per person, a worthwhile splurge)
meals.dinner: Pimatgol Alley pojangmacha – makgeolli, pajeon, and kimchi jeon (kimchi pancake) (~₩12,000–18,000)

day_by_day.notes: Suwon Hwaseong is easily accessible by subway (1 hour from central Seoul). Wear very warm layers – walking the fortress walls in December wind can be bitterly cold. The fortress is illuminated at night for those who stay later. Return to Seoul by 5–6 PM to enjoy the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art (리움미술관) in Hannam-dong – one of Korea's finest private art museums featuring traditional Korean art alongside contemporary international works (~₩20,000). The building itself, designed by three world-renowned architects, is a masterpiece.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Itaewon (이태원) and the adjacent Haebangchon (해방촌) and Hannam-dong neighborhoods – Seoul's most international districts with diverse restaurants, vintage shops, and cultural diversity. Browse the unique boutiques along Usadan-ro and the antique shops of Itaewon's main street.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul is a major celebration. Head to Myeongdong Cathedral (명동성당) for the Christmas Eve mass (one of Asia's most beautiful Gothic cathedrals, open to all). The surrounding Myeongdong area will be dazzling with Christmas lights and festive street food. Seoul celebrates Christmas as a public holiday with spectacular illuminations.

meals.breakfast: Hannam-dong café brunch – Seoul's café culture peaks in this neighborhood; enjoy eggs benedict or Korean-style brunch (~₩12,000–18,000)
meals.lunch: Itaewon international cuisine – try authentic Thai, Indian, or Middle Eastern food for a change of pace (~₩12,000–18,000)
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve special – splurge at a mid-range Korean fusion restaurant in Hannam-dong or Itaewon for a festive dinner (~₩30,000–50,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is one of Seoul's biggest celebrations – the city transforms into a winter wonderland. Myeongdong Cathedral mass is a special experience but gets very crowded; arrive early. Book the dinner restaurant in advance as Christmas Eve is extremely busy. Many couples celebrate Christmas Eve as a romantic holiday in Korean culture.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day is a public holiday in South Korea. Visit the serene Changdeokgung Palace Secret Garden area or take a peaceful morning walk through the snow-dusted streets of Bukchon Hanok Village, which will be quieter than usual. Enjoy the peaceful winter atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Seoul Arts Center (예술의전당) in Seocho – check for special Christmas Day performances (classical concerts, ballet, or opera are common during the holiday season). Alternatively, explore the nearby National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art (MMCA) Seoul branch in the Gyeongbokgung area (~₩4,000).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Lotte World Tower (롯데월드타워) in Jamsil – Seoul's tallest skyscraper with the Seoul Sky observation deck (123rd floor, ~₩29,000). The Christmas illuminations around Lotte World and the adjacent Seokchon Lake are spectacular and one of Seoul's most beloved winter sights. The outdoor ice skating rink at Lotte World is also a fun festive activity (~₩15,000 including skate rental).

meals.breakfast: Hotel or nearby café – treat yourself to a special Christmas morning coffee and pastry (~₩8,000–12,000)
meals.lunch: Traditional Korean holiday food – tteokguk (떡국, rice cake soup) which Koreans traditionally eat on New Year's but is widely available in winter (~₩9,000–13,000)
meals.dinner: Jamsil area near Lotte World – Korean fried chicken (치맥) with beer, a beloved Korean Christmas tradition; try a local chimaek restaurant (~₩20,000–30,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Korean fried chicken with beer (치맥, chimaek) is a beloved Christmas tradition in South Korea. Many Koreans celebrate Christmas with fried chicken and beer rather than a traditional Western meal. The Seokchon Lake Christmas illuminations near Lotte World are free to enjoy and are one of Seoul's most magical seasonal sights.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Mangwon Market (망원시장) – a beloved local neighborhood market popular with young Seoulites, less touristy than Gwangjang Market. Browse fresh produce, local snacks, and street food. Then walk along the Mangwon Hangang Park riverside for winter views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the War Memorial of Korea (전쟁기념관) in Yongsan – a powerful and comprehensive museum documenting Korean military history from ancient times through the Korean War (free entry for permanent collection). The outdoor exhibits include tanks, aircraft, and war monuments. Then explore the adjacent Yongsan Electronics Market – a massive tech shopping complex.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Jongno/Insadong area for a final deep dive into K-culture. Visit a traditional Korean music (gugak) performance if available, or explore the evening tea ceremony experience at one of Insadong's traditional tea houses. Browse the night markets and pick up last-minute souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Mangwon Market street food – freshly made hotteok, tteokbokki, and gimbap for a true local market breakfast experience (~₩5,000–8,000)
meals.lunch: Yongsan area – try a hearty budae jjigae (부대찌개, Korean army stew with sausage, ramen, and vegetables), a uniquely Korean fusion dish born from the Korean War era (~₩12,000–16,000)
meals.dinner: Insadong traditional restaurant – full Korean hansik (한식) dinner with multiple banchan (side dishes), doenjang jjigae, and grilled fish (~₩15,000–22,000)

day_by_day.notes: The War Memorial of Korea is closed on Mondays – open today. Saturday markets are at their liveliest. This is a good day to purchase Korean souvenirs: look for hanji (traditional paper) products, celadon pottery, Korean teas, gochujang paste sets, and K-beauty products in Insadong and Myeongdong.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Seoul. Take a reflective walk back through Gyeongbokgung Palace grounds or the Cheong Wa Dae (청와대, former Blue House presidential residence – now open to public, free). Enjoy the peaceful winter morning atmosphere of the neighborhood you've called home for nearly two weeks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute shopping and souvenir hunting in Insadong or Myeongdong. Visit Olive Young (올리브영) for K-beauty products, and traditional craft shops for authentic Korean gifts. Pack carefully and check out of the hotel. Head to Incheon Airport via AREX Express Train from Seoul Station (allow 2–3 hours before departure).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon International Airport. Enjoy a final Korean meal at the airport – try the food court on the departure level for a last taste of Korean cuisine before flying home.

meals.breakfast: Final Korean breakfast – go back to a favorite restaurant from the trip, or try juk (죽, Korean rice porridge) from Bon Juk for a light, comforting send-off (~₩8,000–12,000)
meals.lunch: Light lunch or snack while finishing shopping – convenience store kimbap and ramyeon for a quintessential Korean experience (~₩4,000–7,000)
meals.dinner: Incheon Airport – Korean restaurant in the departure terminal; try bibimbap or doenjang jjigae for a final authentic taste (~₩12,000–18,000)

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time for airport departure – Incheon Airport recommends arriving 3 hours before international flights. The AREX Express Train from Seoul Station to Incheon Airport takes approximately 43 minutes and runs frequently. You can also do airport check-in at Seoul Station (City Airport Terminal) to drop luggage and clear immigration before boarding the train, saving time at the airport. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Seoul, South Korea Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Incheon International Airport at 13:00 — skip morning activities. Private luxury transfer arranged via premium chauffeur service to your boutique stay in Gyeongbokgung, Jongno-gu. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your hanok-style accommodations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation stroll through the immediate Gyeongbokgung neighborhood. Walk along the iconic Gyeongbokgung Palace outer walls, explore the charming Bukchon Hanok Village entrance lanes just minutes away, and absorb the atmospheric contrast of traditional architecture against the winter sky.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Jungsik (2 Michelin stars, Gangnam) or opt for the closer luxury hanok-dining experience at Jihwaja in Jongno — a royal Korean cuisine restaurant serving authentic joseon-era court food in an elegant setting. Early night to recover from jet lag.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or airport lounge dining
meals.lunch: Light refreshments at hotel upon arrival — request a curated welcome spread of Korean tteok (rice cakes), seasonal fruits, and premium teas from your boutique host
meals.dinner: Jihwaja (지화자) — Royal Korean court cuisine in Jongno; tasting menu featuring gujeolpan, galbi-jjim, and traditional banchan in a refined hanok setting

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport transfer in advance. Ask the hotel concierge for a complimentary neighborhood map and recommendations. Dress warmly — December in Seoul is cold (0–5°C). Jet lag recovery is priority tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Full immersive visit to Gyeongbokgung Palace, steps from your hotel. Arrive early for the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony (10:00 & 14:00). Explore the grand throne hall Geunjeongjeon, the serene Gyeonghoeru Pavilion lake (stunning in winter), and the National Folk Museum of Korea within the palace grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the National Palace Museum of Korea adjacent to the palace for a deep dive into Joseon Dynasty artifacts and royal treasures. Afterward, stroll through Insadong — Seoul's premier cultural street — browsing premium Korean art galleries, antique shops, and craft studios. Visit Ssamziegil courtyard for curated local design.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Bukchon Hanok Village at dusk when the lanterns illuminate the narrow alleys. Then head to Tongin Market area or dine at Gaon (3 Michelin stars) in Gangnam for the pinnacle of Korean fine dining.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — request a traditional Korean morning spread: doenjang-jjigae, steamed rice, assorted banchan, and sikhye (sweet rice drink)
meals.lunch: Balwoo Gongyang (발우공양) in Insadong — award-winning Buddhist temple food (sachal eumsik) served in a meditative, elegant atmosphere; vegetarian tasting menu
meals.dinner: Gaon (가온) — 3 Michelin stars; contemporary Korean haute cuisine with seasonal omakase tasting menu; reserve well in advance

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays — since today is Wednesday, it is open. Wear hanbok (traditional dress) for free palace entry — many rental shops are nearby. Book Gaon reservation at least 2 weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and its UNESCO-listed Secret Garden (Huwon). The winter garden with bare trees and frozen ponds has a hauntingly beautiful aesthetic. Guided tours of the Secret Garden run at specific times — book in advance. Explore the palace's intimate architecture compared to Gyeongbokgung's grandeur.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Changgyeonggung Palace next door, then walk through the historic Ikseon-dong Hanok Village — a trendy yet authentic neighborhood of converted hanok cafés, boutique shops, and artisan studios. Browse luxury Korean craft stores and enjoy the blend of heritage and contemporary Seoul culture.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Naksan Park for panoramic evening views of Seoul's city lights and the illuminated Seoul City Wall. Dine in the upscale Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) area or return to Jongno for an intimate dinner.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast with seasonal Korean porridge (juk) — pumpkin or abalone juk with side dishes
meals.lunch: Ikseon-dong neighborhood — dine at a premium hanok café-restaurant such as Ikseon Galbi serving premium short-rib set meals in a beautifully restored hanok
meals.dinner: Mingles (밍글스) — 2 Michelin stars in Gangnam; innovative Korean fusion cuisine blending traditional ingredients with modern technique; exceptional wine pairing available

day_by_day.notes: Secret Garden guided tours are limited — book online at the Cultural Heritage Administration website. Bring hand warmers for outdoor exploration. Ikseon-dong is best explored on foot.

day_by_day.morning: Immerse in K-culture with a private Korean cooking class hosted by a master chef in a traditional hanok kitchen. Learn to prepare royal court dishes: japchae, kimchi, tteokguk, and haemul pajeon. This hands-on cultural experience is both educational and deeply personal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan — one of Asia's largest museums with extraordinary collections of Silla gold crowns, Goryeo celadon, and Joseon paintings. Explore at a leisurely premium pace. Afterward, walk through the beautifully landscaped museum grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Namsan Seoul Tower (N Seoul Tower) at dusk — take the cable car up and enjoy the glittering winter cityscape. The observation deck at night is magical. Dine at the N Grill revolving restaurant at the top for a 360° panoramic fine dining experience.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — request haemul-juk (seafood porridge) with premium side dishes
meals.lunch: Enjoy the fruits of your morning cooking class — a curated sit-down meal of everything you prepared, served formally
meals.dinner: N Grill at Namsan Tower — revolving fine dining with French-Korean fusion cuisine; panoramic Seoul views; premium wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book the private cooking class through your hotel concierge or services like O'ngo Food Communications. Reserve N Grill in advance — window seats fill quickly. Cable car to Namsan runs until late evening.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the UNESCO World Heritage site of Suwon Hwaseong Fortress (45 min by KTX/taxi from central Seoul). Walk the stunning 5.7km fortress wall circuit in the crisp winter air — the ramparts, watchtowers, and gates are spectacular. Visit Hwaseong Haenggung (detached palace) within the fortress.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Seoul and explore the vibrant Hongdae neighborhood — the epicenter of Korean youth culture, street art, indie music, and K-pop. Visit the Line Friends flagship store, explore concept stores, and browse the creative underground culture scene. Experience a live busking performance if available.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the upscale Sinchon/Mapo area for dinner, then experience a premium K-pop culture event — visit SM Town COEX Artium or HYBE Insight museum for an immersive K-pop cultural experience (book tickets in advance).

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — traditional Korean spread with doenjang-jjigae and grilled fish
meals.lunch: Suwon Galbi (수원갈비) — Suwon is famous for its premium short-rib galbi; dine at a renowned local galbi restaurant near Hwaseong for an authentic regional specialty
meals.dinner: Onjium (온지음) in Jongno — sophisticated Korean traditional cuisine research restaurant; seasonal tasting menu rooted in historical Korean culinary heritage

day_by_day.notes: Suwon is easily reached by subway (Line 1) or taxi. Hwaseong Fortress is partially illuminated at night if you return late. HYBE Insight requires advance ticket booking online.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Seongbuk-dong neighborhood — one of Seoul's most exclusive and culturally rich residential areas. Visit Gilsangsa Temple, a serene urban Buddhist temple with beautiful winter gardens donated by a restaurateur. Stroll through the quiet, upscale streets past embassies and traditional estates.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Whanki Museum (환기미술관) — a world-class private museum dedicated to Korean abstract artist Kim Whanki, set in a stunning architectural building in Buam-dong. Then explore Buam-dong's boutique cafés and art spaces — one of Seoul's most refined and under-the-radar neighborhoods.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Korean performing arts show — the National Gugak Center in Seocho offers premium performances of court music, pansori, and traditional dance. Book VIP seating for the best experience.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — request a premium juk (porridge) course with abalone and seasonal vegetables
meals.lunch: Buam-dong neighborhood café-restaurant — try Sanmotoonge or a similar upscale café with Korean fusion brunch in a scenic hillside setting
meals.dinner: Jungsik (정식당) — 2 Michelin stars; pioneering New Korean Cuisine; creative seasonal tasting menu with exceptional wine and makgeolli pairing; elegant contemporary setting

day_by_day.notes: Gilsangsa Temple is free to enter and offers a peaceful contrast to the busy city. Check the National Gugak Center performance schedule in advance at gugak.go.kr. Buam-dong is best reached by taxi.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury day trip to Nami Island (남이섬) and Petite France in Gapyeong County (1.5 hrs from Seoul). Nami Island in winter is ethereally beautiful — bare silver birch trees, frost on the ground, and quiet serenity. Famous as a filming location for the K-drama 'Winter Sonata.'
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the nearby Garden of Morning Calm (아침고요수목원) — Korea's oldest private arboretum, which hosts a spectacular winter illumination festival in December called 'Lighting Festival.' The illuminated garden paths through snow-dusted trees are breathtaking.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul by private transfer. Relax at your boutique hotel with an in-room premium Korean skincare ritual or arrange a traditional Korean jjimjilbang (luxury spa) experience at a premium bathhouse.

meals.breakfast: Early in-hotel breakfast before departure — light Korean spread
meals.lunch: On Nami Island — the island has several restaurants; opt for the premium Nami Island Restaurant with river views and Korean set menus
meals.dinner: La Yeon (라연) at The Shilla Hotel — 3 Michelin stars; the pinnacle of Korean fine dining; exquisite seasonal tasting menu in a refined setting with views over Namsan; one of Asia's best restaurants

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private car/driver for the Nami Island day trip through your hotel concierge for maximum comfort. Garden of Morning Calm winter festival runs November–January. La Yeon reservation is essential — book 1 month ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art — one of Asia's finest private art museums, designed by three legendary architects (Mario Botta, Jean Nouvel, Rem Koolhaas). The collection spans ancient Korean treasures to contemporary global art. A must for culture enthusiasts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon in Itaewon and the adjacent Hannam-dong neighborhood — Seoul's most cosmopolitan and upscale district. Browse premium concept stores, international designer boutiques, and Korean luxury brands. Visit the flagship stores of Gentle Monster (luxury eyewear/art installations) and Tamburins.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a premium Korean BBQ dinner — not just any BBQ, but a high-end hanwoo (Korean wagyu) experience. Then explore Itaewon's sophisticated cocktail bar scene.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — full traditional Korean morning meal with grilled mackerel, rice, miso soup, and 12 banchan
meals.lunch: Hannam-dong neighborhood — dine at Mosu Seoul (1 Michelin star) for inventive Korean-inspired tasting menus with global influences
meals.dinner: Hanwoo Club (한우클럽) or Dalsaem (달샘) — premium hanwoo Korean beef BBQ restaurant; A++ grade wagyu grilled tableside; private dining room available; exceptional soju and wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Leeum Museum may have temporary closures — verify hours in advance. Hannam-dong is very walkable and is considered Seoul's most upscale lifestyle district. Book private dining room at the BBQ restaurant for an exclusive experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple — the head temple of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism, located in the heart of Jongno. In December, the temple is decorated with thousands of colorful lanterns for the winter season, creating a magical atmosphere. Participate in a morning temple stay program or simply observe the morning rituals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Cheonggyecheon Stream — a beautifully restored urban waterway running through central Seoul. Walk along the elevated stream path and visit the Cheong Gye Plaza. Then head to the nearby Gwanghwamun Square to see the statues of King Sejong and Admiral Yi Sun-sin with Gyeongbokgung as a backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a performance at the Seoul Arts Center (예술의전당) in Seocho — Korea's premier performing arts venue. Check the December schedule for classical music concerts, opera, or ballet performances. Pre-purchase premium seats.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — request a temple-food-inspired breakfast: simple, clean, vegetarian Korean morning meal
meals.lunch: Tosokchon Samgyetang (토속촌) — famous premium ginseng chicken soup restaurant near Gyeongbokgung; warming and restorative in winter; a Seoul institution
meals.dinner: Pre-theater dinner at Bicena (비체나) near Seoul Arts Center — elegant contemporary Korean cuisine; seasonal menu; excellent wine list; popular with Seoul's cultural elite

day_by_day.notes: Jogyesa Temple is free to enter. The lantern decorations are especially beautiful after dark — consider returning for an evening stroll. Seoul Arts Center schedule available at sac.or.kr — book VIP seats.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Gyeonghuigung Palace (경희궁) — the least visited of Seoul's five grand palaces, offering a peaceful and uncrowded experience. Then explore the Seoul Museum of History adjacent to it for a comprehensive understanding of Seoul's urban development from ancient times to modernity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury shopping experience in Gangnam — visit the Hyundai Department Store The Hyundai Seoul or Lotte World Mall for premium Korean and international brands. Explore K-beauty at its finest: visit Amorepacific flagship store, Sulwhasoo Flagship, and curated K-beauty concept stores. Personal shopping assistant can be arranged.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve celebration — Seoul transforms beautifully for Christmas. Join the festive atmosphere around Myeongdong Cathedral (one of Korea's most iconic Christmas landmarks) for the midnight mass or evening service. The surrounding streets are adorned with spectacular light installations.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — special Christmas Eve morning spread; request seasonal Korean-Western fusion breakfast
meals.lunch: Gangnam luxury dining — Sushi Saito Seoul (if available) or Pierre Gagnaire à Séoul at Lotte Hotel for a premium French-Korean Christmas Eve lunch experience
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve tasting menu at Jung Sik Dang or book a private dining experience at your hotel — many luxury hotels offer exclusive Christmas Eve multi-course dinners with wine pairing and live music

day_by_day.notes: Christmas is widely celebrated in South Korea. Myeongdong Cathedral midnight mass is a cultural highlight — arrive early for seating. Many restaurants offer special Christmas Eve menus — book well in advance. The city lights are spectacular tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas morning luxury experience — sleep in and enjoy a premium in-hotel brunch. Afterward, visit Bukhansan National Park (북한산국립공원) at the northern edge of Seoul for a scenic winter hike. The snow-dusted granite peaks and pine forests are spectacular. Choose a manageable trail like Bukhansanseong Fortress trail for stunning views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and visit Ihwa Mural Village (이화동) on the slopes of Naksan — a charming artistic neighborhood with murals, galleries, and independent studios. The hillside views over Jongno are beautiful. Then relax at a premium Korean spa (jjimjilbang) — try Spa Lei or Dragon Hill Spa for a luxury wellness experience.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas dinner at one of Seoul's most celebrated restaurants — a truly special occasion meal to mark the holiday.

meals.breakfast: Luxurious in-hotel Christmas brunch — eggs benedict, smoked salmon, Korean rice cakes, premium pastries, champagne
meals.lunch: Light mountain café stop during or after the hike — many cafés near Bukhansan entrance serve excellent Korean street food and hot drinks
meals.dinner: Kwon Sooksoo (권숙수) — 2 Michelin stars; intimate, refined Korean cuisine by Chef Kwon Woo-joong; exceptional seasonal tasting menu; one of Seoul's most personal fine dining experiences; Christmas special menu

day_by_day.notes: Bukhansan trails can be icy in December — bring proper hiking shoes with grip or rent crampons near the park entrance. Dragon Hill Spa is open 24 hours and is a quintessential Korean cultural experience. Book Christmas dinner reservation far in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final full-day deep dive into K-culture. Visit the K-Wave (Hallyu) experience at COEX — explore SM Town COEX Artium's interactive K-pop museum, hologram theater, and exclusive merchandise. Then visit the nearby COEX Starfield Library — one of Seoul's most Instagrammable spaces, a stunning two-story library inside a mall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Apgujeong Rodeo Street and Cheongdam-dong — Seoul's most exclusive luxury fashion district, often called 'the Korean Beverly Hills.' Visit the Chanel flagship, Dior Maison, and Korean luxury designer boutiques. Explore the Galleria Department Store's luxury wing. Visit the Gentle Monster House Dosan flagship — a surrealist art-meets-eyewear concept store.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell to the Hanok neighborhood — take a final golden-hour walk through Bukchon Hanok Village as the lanterns come on. Soak in the beauty of the traditional rooftop silhouettes against the winter sky. Farewell dinner at Seoul's most prestigious address.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — full traditional Korean spread; savor every last banchan
meals.lunch: Cheongdam-dong — dine at Ryunique (류니크) for creative contemporary Korean cuisine in an intimate chef's table setting; innovative seasonal menu
meals.dinner: La Yeon (라연) at The Shilla Hotel (if not visited on Day 7) OR Soil (소일) — a new-generation Korean fine dining restaurant celebrating Korean terroir; exquisite farewell dinner with premium Korean wine and spirits pairing

day_by_day.notes: COEX Artium SM Town requires advance ticket booking. Cheongdam-dong boutiques may require appointments for premium brands. This is your final evening in the Bukchon area — take time to appreciate the neighborhood that has been your home base.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Seoul — wake up early for one last sunrise walk along the Gyeongbokgung Palace walls. The quiet winter morning with the palace and mountains behind it is a perfect farewell image. Visit the Gyeongbokgung gift shop for premium souvenirs: high-quality Korean ceramics, silk goods, and traditional crafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time — last-minute shopping at Insadong for premium Korean teas, hanji (traditional paper) goods, and artisan ceramics. Pack and check out of your boutique hanok stay. Private luxury transfer to Incheon International Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon. Enjoy the premium airport experience — Incheon is consistently rated the world's best airport. Visit the Korean Cultural Street on the transit level, enjoy a final Korean meal at the airport's premium restaurant options, and relax in the First Class lounge.

meals.breakfast: Final in-hotel breakfast — a mindful, unhurried Korean morning meal to close the journey; request a special farewell spread from your host
meals.lunch: Insadong area — light farewell lunch at Sanchon (산촌), a renowned temple food restaurant serving vegetarian Buddhist cuisine in a beautiful hanok setting
meals.dinner: Incheon Airport — dine at one of the premium airport restaurants or enjoy Korean snacks and teas in the First Class lounge before your flight

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure at Incheon. The airport has excellent duty-free shopping for last-minute K-beauty and Korean spirits purchases. Korean Air and Asiana First Class lounges are exceptional. Safe travels!

query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter 2026 from LAX
